newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA FINANCES WHEAT PURCHASE AND STORAGE.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA FINANCES WHEAT PURCHASE AND STORAGE.

text.p: Romania's government has granted credits and subsidies equivalent to $90 million to a newly liberalised market for buying and storing a forecast bumper grain crop, the Agriculture Ministry said on Thursday.
The measures include a fund of 500 billion lei for domestic wheat purchases and subsidies worth 150 billion lei for storage.
The reformist government earlier this year liberalised bread prices, eliminated a fixed floor rate and ended a state monopoly on grain purchases and storage.
"We wanted to make sure that there is enough liquidity to allow the purchase of wheat," Agriculture Ministry Secretary of State Aurel Pana said by telephone.
Pana said the 500 billion lei would be available as a revolving soft credit for grain traders and milling companies.
The additional 150 billion lei would allow free storage of two million tonnes of wheat for eight months to maintain grain in proper conditions as farmers set about selling it.
The farming ministry expects a 1997 wheat crop of 7.07 million tonnes and plans to export 2.4 million. Romania harvested 3.1 million tonnes of wheat in 1996.
But Pana said the costs of bringing in a tonne of wheat varied, making some locally made flour more expensive than imported varieties.
